name: Software Factory
tagline: Small delivery loops on a Raspberry Pi, with human approval and verified changes.
headline:
Small loops.
Real checks.
One Raspberry Pi.
summary: A production delivery system that reviews pull requests, ships verified changes, watches the logs and turns approved tickets into small repairs. The Pi edits files; GitHub Actions builds and tests. I choose what the agent takes on and merge sensitive changes myself.

statement.label: Why I built it
statement.text: Running this site gave me the same repetitive work as a larger service: review a change, check the build, deploy it, watch for errors and deal with dependency findings. I wanted a system that closes those small loops and leaves its decisions visible.

points.title: The constraint
points.text: A Raspberry Pi 5 already hosts the production stack. Code edits happen there; builds, dependency downloads and tests run on GitHub Actions.

points.title: The loops
points.text: Review, merge, deploy and observe; report a vulnerability; turn an approved ticket into a checked repair; carry review lessons forward.

points.title: The gate
points.text: Checks and review conversations must be clear. Infrastructure, dependency edits and changes that silence a symptom require a person to merge.

points.title: The decisions
points.text: Machines do the noticing, ticketing, checking and routine shipping. I decide which tickets become work and which sensitive changes reach production.

highlights.title: The Pi edits; GitHub verifies
highlights.text: A file-only ticket agent proposes small changes without building or downloading dependencies on the production host. GitHub Actions and the reviewer judge the exact commit.
highlights.imageAlt: Diagram separating file edits on the Raspberry Pi from builds and tests on GitHub Actions.

highlights.title: A visible repair loop
highlights.text: An approved Linear ticket becomes a pull request. A red check becomes the next brief, with three attempts in total. In Review means green checks; Done means merged.
highlights.imageAlt: Ticket repair loop showing approval, file edits, CI, the repair budget and the merge.

highlights.title: Sensitive merges stay human
highlights.text: Dependency and build changes carry no-auto-merge, as do changes that silence a warning or disable a check. The npm lockfile limitation is documented rather than hidden.
highlights.imageAlt: CVE swimlane with the person approving the scoped fix and merging its dependency pull request.

demo.title: Small loops on a Raspberry Pi
demo.summary: The hardware constraint, the worker and deployer boundaries, and the production console connecting review, deployment, logwatch and approved ticket repairs.

pages.summary: How reviews, deploys, logwatch, vulnerability reports and approved repairs connect, and where a person decides.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: One factory container, an isolated deployer, durable role queues and builds on GitHub Actions.
